item.title: Chef Said On A Plate
item.description: Personal chef and co-host of The Desert Brew, Chef Said, cooks us kafta with potatoes. We talk about his journey into food, his Lebanese roots and inspirations, his architectural design to plating, and of course his famous spice suitcase with flavors from all over the world. This is Chef Said on a plate. For more Coachella Valley News visit NBCPalmSprings.com

item.title: Signs of Fascism Rally Held in Indio Saturday
item.description: Democrats in Sun City Shadow Hills gathered Saturday morning for a protest aimed at raising awareness about what organizers call signs of fascism in the United States.The demonstration began around 10 a.m. in the Food 4 Less parking lot at the corner of Monroe Street and Highway 111 in Indio. item.title: More Americans Turning to Entrepreneurship as Small Business Ownership Rises
item.description: A growing number of Americans are choosing to become their own boss, with new studies showing a significant increase in small business startups across the country.NBC Palm Springs’ Kai Beech spoke with local entrepreneur Sue Moss, who is starting her business from scratch after making a major career shift. item.title: Left-Leaning Gun Groups See Surge in Membership Following Minneapolis Shooting and Federal Enforcement Actions
item.description: Left-leaning gun advocacy groups across the country say they are experiencing a dramatic increase in membership and firearms training requests following the killing of Alex Pretti by federal agents in Minneapolis.Organizations such as the Liberal Gun Club and Pink Pistols Twin Cities report sold-out classes and expanded schedules as more liberals, LGBTQ individuals, women, and people of color seek gun education and permits. item.description: The U.S. Justice Department is signaling it will not bring additional charges connected to the investigation into Jeffrey Epstein, according to Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche.Speaking on CNN’s State of the Union, Blanche said federal officials have reviewed millions of pages of documents tied to Epstein and determined there is not enough evidence to prosecute anyone else. item.title: Rising Crime and Political Apathy Shape Costa Rica’s Presidential Election as Voters Head to the Polls
item.description: Voters in Costa Rica are heading to the polls to elect a new president after a campaign season marked by rising crime, economic inequality, and growing political disengagement.In the capital city of San José, analysts say public concern over security now outweighs nearly every other issue. item.title: Amazon Touts Box Office Success of “Melania” Documentary, Though Film Remains Far From Profitable
item.description: Amazon is highlighting a strong opening weekend for the documentary “Melania,” though financial analysts say the film remains well short of turning a profit.The project, produced by Amazon MGM Studios, is projected to earn about $7 million in its debut weekend — an impressive figure for a documentary. item.title: Retired Astronauts Share Their Favorite Space Movies as NASA’s Artemis II Puts Moon Missions Back in the Spotlight
item.description: As NASA prepares for its Artemis II mission — expected to launch as early as February 6 — human spaceflight is once again capturing public imagination.
